extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers for Elsevier journals (academic researchers who review manuscripts)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for academic reviewers on how to evaluate and report on submitted journal manuscripts (research and review article types) for Elsevier journals, including ethical, methodological, and presentation-related criteria. Covers pre-acceptance considerations, managing the review, structured prompts for different article types, finalizing the report, and post-review obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the article match your area of expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Only accept if you feel you can provide a high-quality review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before accepting/declining an invitation, confirm the manuscript falls within your expertise; only accept when you can provide a thorough, high-quality assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you have a potential conflict of interest? Disclose this to the editor when you respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any potential conflicts exist (financial, personal, professional), inform the editor immediately so they can reassign or advise. Do not review if conflict precludes impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you have time? Reviewing can be a lot of work — before you commit, make sure you can meet the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only accept invitations when you can meet the review deadline. If you must decline, respond promptly and suggest alternative reviewers if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond promptly to invitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to the invitation as soon as you can (even if it is to decline) — a delay in your decision slows down the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt acceptance or decline helps editorial workflow; when declining, provide suggestions for alternative reviewers where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat submission materials as confidential
rubrics_metrics.description: If you accept, you must treat the materials you receive as confidential documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not share manuscripts, data, or review content with anyone without prior authorization from the editor. Do not discuss the review publicly unless the journal has an explicit policy allowing it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI and reviewer responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers or editors should not upload the manuscript or any part of it into a Generative AI tool; Generative AI should not be used to assist in the review, evaluation or decision-making process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use generative AI for reviewing or decision-making; do not upload manuscripts or peer-review reports into AI tools (privacy/data use risk). Editors may use identity-protected AI screening tools that conform to RELX Responsible AI Principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarize with journal-specific guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: When you sit down to write the review, make sure you familiarize yourself with any journal-specific guidelines (these will be noted in the journal’s guide for authors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the target journal’s instructions for reviewers/guide for authors and follow any specific formats, questionnaires, or reporting standards requested by the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide supported judgements
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing insight into any deficiencies is important. You should explain and support your judgement so that both editors and authors are able to fully understand the reasoning behind your comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why you judge aspects as deficient or acceptable, indicate when a comment is opinion versus evidenced by data, and give constructive suggestions for improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title accuracy and discoverability
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the title accurately and sufficiently describes the content. You may want to factor in discoverability/searchability of the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the title reflects the study's scope, methods, and key findings; recommend including study type (e.g., RCT) where appropriate for clarity and discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract completeness and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the abstract accurately reflects all essential aspects of the study, including all major results and limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the abstract summarizes objectives, methods, primary results, and key limitations; it should be a stand-alone summary that mirrors the manuscript content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction: background, rationale, and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The background and literature section should be up-to-date and appropriate for the topic. The introduction should clearly explain the scientific background and rationale of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that literature cited is current and relevant, the rationale for the study is clear, and primary/secondary objectives are stated (ideally at the end of the introduction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: detail for replication and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The study methods, which include the theory, applicability, and modeling, should be described in sufficient detail to enable replication and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that study design is identified (RCT, cohort, case-control, cross-sectional), population is described, sample size estimation is detailed, and rationale (including MCID) is literature-backed. Ensure controls, sampling mechanisms, statistical reporting (p-values, confidence intervals, effect sizes) are described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analyses: appropriateness and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical analyses such as controls, sampling mechanisms, and statistical reporting (e.g., p-values, CIs, effect sizes, etc.) should be appropriately described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether chosen statistical methods match the study questions, check adequacy of power/sample size, appropriateness of controls and sampling, and that results include relevant metrics like CIs and effect sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: presentation and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify whether the presentation of the results, including the number of tables and figures, are appropriate to best visualize the findings of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check clarity and sufficiency of tables/figures, consistency with text, and whether additional sub-analyses (CIs, effect sizes, sensitivity analyses) are needed for transparency and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion: interpretations and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The interpretation of the results and study conclusions should be supported by the data and study design. Assess whether the authors have clearly emphasized the limitations of their study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure authors do not overstate findings, link conclusions to presented data and methods, and clearly identify study limitations (theory, methods, generalizability).

rubrics_metrics.name: References: currency and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Scrutinize whether the references used in this study are the most up-to-date and relevant for the topic at hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for missing foundational or recent studies, suggest additions, and check balanced citation of competing groups and important work in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language quality and readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the manuscript would benefit from professional language editing or improvements in grammar, clarity, or readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If language impedes comprehension, recommend professional editing; provide brief, constructive suggestions for clarity but avoid focusing on copyediting if research is sound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall assessment of novelty, importance, and contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: State if this paper presents research that is novel or important for the journal or for the field, and whether it contributes to the educational goals of the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize the manuscript’s significance, originality, reproducibility, and fit for the journal; flag ethical or integrity concerns for editorial attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review article: rationale and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the authors clearly explain the rationale for writing a review article in this field and justify the need and relevance of the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend ways authors can better justify the review’s contribution or scope, and whether it addresses a gap or synthesizes literature meaningfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review article: historical development and future insights
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the review provides a comprehensive overview of the historical development of the field while also offering insights into its future directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify missing historical milestones or future trends that should be included or emphasized to strengthen the review’s perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review references and coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the authors adequately discuss the most relevant and recent advances, including coverage of all or most relevant research groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend additions for key topics, foundational studies, or recent publications; check for balanced coverage across research groups and perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods and reproducibility for reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the review is reported with sufficient methodological detail to allow replicability or reproducibility (e.g., clear search strategies, inclusion/exclusion criteria, risk-of-bias assessments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask for transparent reporting of search methods, selection criteria, data extraction, and any bias assessment; recommend adherence to standard methods for systematic reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods in reviews/meta-analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether any statistical methods used (e.g., meta-analysis, meta-regression) are appropriate and clearly described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check reporting of p-values, 95% CIs, heterogeneity measures; indicate whether a statistician’s review would be beneficial and suggest improvements to analysis or reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential reporting requirements and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the overall structure, flow, and clarity of the manuscript; suggest improvements such as reorganizing subheadings or aligning with reporting standards (e.g., PRISMA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend structural edits, adherence to discipline-specific reporting guidelines, and improvements to flow and clarity to aid reproducibility and reader comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex and gender reporting (SAGER-related checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess manuscripts for inclusion of sex-disaggregated data and gender analysis, and adherence to guidance such as SAGER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check use of terms 'sex' vs 'gender' and definitions, whether sex of participants is defined and reported (self-report or assignment), reporting for animal/cell studies (sex of animals or cell origin), justification where only one sex included, disaggregation of data by sex/gender or explanation for lack thereof, request subgroup analyses if needed, and require discussion of limitations and generalizability regarding sex/gender aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research data and visualization scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: Once methodology is robust, examine any data in the form of figures, tables, or images; research data and data visualizations should receive attention during review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check linked data and database identifiers; identify critical data flaws such as insufficient data points, statistically non-significant variations presented as meaningful, or unclear data tables; use available preview tools for certain visualizations and recommend better visualization or data provision where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical considerations and approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments including patient or animal data should properly be documented and usually require ethical approval by the author’s host organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify documented ethical approvals, consent procedures, animal welfare statements, and compliance with journal-specific ethics policies; flag any concerns to the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone, professionalism, and constructive language
rubrics_metrics.description: Your comments should be courteous and constructive, and should not include any ad hominem remarks or personal details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use professional, objective language; avoid personal attacks; be clear which comments are for the editor vs for the authors; respect confidentiality and any identity-transparency policies of the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of reviewer comments and readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize the article in a short paragraph; use short, clearly-defined paragraphs and make it easy to see what section you’re referring to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with a concise summary, then list major and minor points, use section-referenced comments, and ensure readability so editors and authors can quickly understand your main impressions and actionable suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on substantive issues over copyediting
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t feel the need to comment on spelling, grammar or layout. If the research is sound, but let down by poor language, then recommend language editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize scientific validity, methods, analyses, and interpretation. Recommend professional language editing when necessary rather than exhaustive copyediting in the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inappropriate citation suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggesting that the author include citations to your (or your associates’) work is discouraged unless for genuine scientific reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not suggest citations for the purpose of increasing your own citation count or visibility; recommend citations only when they materially improve the manuscript’s context or completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain confidentiality of review content
rubrics_metrics.description: Share the review or information about the review with anyone without the agreement of the editors and authors involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per COPE guidelines, treat manuscripts and reviews as confidential during and after the process unless the journal publishes peer review comments or gives permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raise ethical concerns with supporting detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Raise your suspicions with the editor if you suspect plagiarism or research falsification or have other ethical concerns, providing as much detail as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report suspected misconduct privately to the editor with specific evidence and examples; consult Elsevier’s ethics page or COPE guidelines for procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of and mitigate unconscious bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of potential bias in your review. Unconscious bias can lead to questionable decisions that negatively impact the academic publishing process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflect on potential biases (e.g., institutional, geographic, gender) and focus on objective assessment criteria; avoid dismissing alternative viewpoints simply because they differ from your perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation types and explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a decision recommendation type (Reject, Accept without revision, Revise — either major or minor) and explain your reasoning in your report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recommending revision, explain required changes and indicate whether you would be willing to review the revised manuscript; provide clear rationale to help the editor weigh your recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-review: continued confidentiality and reviewer recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not share the article and any linked files or data as confidential documents. Use Elsevier’s Reviewer Hub to receive credit for your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain confidentiality after submission of your review; consider registering with Reviewer Hub for recognition, certificates, and private profile of review activity if desired.
